title: Python Programming
description: Computational thinking, Python programming, control flow, functions, file handling, modules, packages, data structures, searching, and sorting.

modules.title: Unit I: Computational Thinking and Problem Solving

lessons.title: Fundamentals of Computing and Computational Problems
lessons.content:
Fundamentals of Computing and Identification of Computational Problems

Learn the fundamentals of computing and how to identify computational problems, including inputs, outputs, constraints, assumptions, and expected results.

Learning resources

  • Fundamentals of Computing Notes
  • Computational Problems Notes

Sample program concept

No sample program. Focus on identifying the problem, input, processing, and output.

lessons.title: Algorithms and Building Blocks of Algorithms
lessons.content:
Algorithms and Building Blocks of Algorithms

Study statements, state, control flow, functions, decomposition, and the role of notation in algorithm design.

What is an Algorithm? - GeeksforGeeks

Sample program concepts

  1. Write an algorithm to add two numbers.
  2. Write an algorithm to find the largest of two numbers.
  3. Write an algorithm to check whether a number is even or odd.
  4. Write an algorithm to check whether a number is positive, negative, or zero.
  5. Write an algorithm to calculate the area of a circle.

lessons.title: Notation Challenge: Pseudo-code, Flowcharts and Programming Languages
lessons.content:
Notation: Pseudo-code, Flowcharts and Programming Languages

Learn how the same algorithm can be represented using pseudo-code, flowcharts, and a programming language.

Learning resources

  • What is PseudoCode - GeeksforGeeks
  • Introduction to Flowcharts - GeeksforGeeks
  • Introduction to Programming Languages - GeeksforGeeks

Pseudo-code tasks

  1. Calculate the area of a rectangle.
  2. Calculate the total marks of three subjects.
  3. Calculate the average marks of three subjects.
  4. Check whether a student has passed or failed.

Flowchart tasks

  1. Calculate the final bill amount after discount.
  2. Convert Celsius to Fahrenheit.
  3. Calculate the salary after adding a bonus.

challenge.prompt: Write pseudo-code for one of the listed tasks. Include clear input, processing, decision, and output steps. You may then open the related flowchart task.

lessons.title: Flowchart Challenge: Represent an Algorithm
lessons.content:
Create a Flowchart

Create a flowchart for one of the Unit I tasks: final bill after discount, Celsius to Fahrenheit conversion, or salary after adding a bonus.

Use standard flowchart notation and connect every step in execution order.

challenge.prompt: Build the flow in execution order using start, input, process, decision where required, output, and end nodes.

lessons.title: Algorithmic Problem Solving, Iteration and Recursion
lessons.content:
Algorithmic Problem Solving and Strategies

Practice decomposition, iteration, recursion, tracing, testing, and improving algorithms.

Algorithmic Problem Solving Notes

Iteration and Recursion Notes

Sample program concepts

  1. Write a Python program to find the factorial of a number using iteration.
  2. Write a Python program to find the nth Fibonacci number using recursion.

lessons.title: Iteration and Recursion Challenge
lessons.content:
Iteration and Recursion Challenge

Write the algorithm or pseudo-code for both sample tasks: factorial using iteration and nth Fibonacci number using recursion.

challenge.prompt: Submit a clear solution plan for factorial using iteration and Fibonacci using recursion. Include the recursive base case and the loop state.
